```{r setup}
library(arrow); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr)
library(stringr); library(scales); library(gt); library(here); library(glue)
options(arrow.skip_nul = TRUE)

ANALYSIS <- here("phase2", "data", "analysis", "deliverable06")
OUTPUT   <- here("phase2", "output", "deliverable06")
FIGS     <- file.path(OUTPUT, "figures")

verdicts <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "candidate_verdicts.parquet"))
clusters <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "ce_clusters.parquet"))
ce_land  <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "ce_landscape_ces.parquet"))
corp     <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "candidate_corpus.parquet"))
facts    <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "candidate_facts.parquet"))
inv      <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "fonsi_project_inventory.parquet"))

corp_fonsi  <- corp |> filter(is_fonsi)
n_clean     <- inv |> filter(project_energy_type == "Clean") |> distinct(project_id) |> nrow()
n_candidate <- corp_fonsi |> distinct(project_id) |> nrow()
n_ce_shaped <- corp_fonsi |> filter(is_profile_subtype) |> distinct(project_id) |> nrow()
n_other     <- n_clean - n_candidate

n_new   <- sum(verdicts$verdict == "new")
n_adopt <- sum(verdicts$verdict == "adopt")
n_ce    <- nrow(ce_land)
n_units <- n_distinct(ce_land$agency_unit)
n_xdup  <- sum(ce_land$xagency_near_duplicate, na.rm = TRUE)
n_xclust <- sum(clusters$n_agencies >= 2)
```

## What this is — and why FONSIs

This is technical support for **categorical-exclusion (CE) development**: which
recurring clean-energy actions, drawn from real federal review records, point to
a CE opportunity? Under CEQ's April 2026 CE guidance, a prior Environmental
Assessment that ended in a **Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI)** is
explicit, citable evidence for establishing a CE — the agency did the full
analysis and concluded the action does *not* significantly affect the
environment. A pile of FONSIs for the *same kind of action* is exactly the
substantiation a new or borrowed CE needs.

So we start from every clean-energy FONSI, narrow to the actions that actually
look like a CE (bounded, low-impact, recurring), and check each one against the
**entire existing federal CE catalog** to see whether it is genuinely new, or
already excluded somewhere.

## How we got here

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "The narrowing from all clean-energy FONSIs to CE candidates."
#| out-width: 92%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_funnel.png"))
```

From **`r n_clean` clean-energy EA→FONSI projects**, `r n_candidate` fall into one
of five recognizable candidate action types; **`r n_ce_shaped`** of those are
"CE-shaped" — bounded and low-impact enough to plausibly be a CE. We then
cross-referenced every candidate against the **`r comma(n_ce)` existing federal
CEs** (CE Explorer catalog, `r n_units` agency units).

## The headline

> **Every CE-shaped clean-energy candidate we found already maps to an existing
> categorical exclusion. None is net-new (`r n_new`).** The opportunity in this
> set is not to *invent* CEs — it is to **adopt and harmonize** CEs that already
> exist at one agency so the others doing the same work can use them.

That is a real, actionable finding: agencies are spending full EAs on actions
that a peer agency has already determined deserve a categorical exclusion.

## The opportunity: adopt existing CEs

```{r adopt-table}
url_for <- function(id) {
  u <- ce_land$canonical_source_url[match(id, ce_land$structured_id)]
  ifelse(is.na(u) | u == "", id, glue("[{id}]({u})"))
}

verdicts |>
  filter(verdict == "adopt") |>
  arrange(desc(rank_score)) |>
  transmute(
    Action = str_replace(candidate_label, " \\(.*\\)", ""),
    `CE-shaped FONSIs` = n_profile_fonsi,
    `Existing CE` = vapply(best_ce_structured_id, url_for, character(1)),
    `Held by` = best_ce_agency,
    `Agencies that could adopt it` = adopt_targets,
    States = n_states
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = `Existing CE`) |>
  tab_header(title = "Adopt-an-existing-CE opportunities",
             subtitle = "Clean-energy actions already excluded at one agency, run as full EAs at others") |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), column_labels.font.weight = "bold")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "How many agencies could adopt an existing CE, by action."
#| out-width: 88%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_adoption_gap.png"))
```

Each row is the same pattern: a CE for the action exists (the *Held by* agency),
but other agencies are running the identical action through a full EA→FONSI and
could adopt it. The match is an embedding-ranked candidate, so the specific CE
should be confirmed against its eCFR text before action.

## Worked example: transmission upgrades within existing right-of-way

The strongest-evidenced case. **`r verdicts$n_profile_fonsi[verdicts$candidate_category=="transmission_upgrade"]`
CE-shaped FONSIs** for in-corridor transmission upgrades (reconductoring,
component replacement, minor rebuilds), spread across **BLM, DOE, NNSA, and the
power-marketing administrations** in **`r verdicts$n_states[verdicts$candidate_category=="transmission_upgrade"]`
states**. The **Tennessee Valley Authority already holds a CE** for exactly this
class of work:

> *TVA CE #17 — "Routine modification, repair, and maintenance of, and minor
> upgrade of and addition to, existing transmission infrastructure …
> transmission line uprate, modification, reconductoring, and clearance
> resolution …"*

These other agencies are doing the same in-ROW upgrades the long way. A sample of
the underlying FONSIs (full citations in the project records):

```{r transmission-example}
tx <- facts |>
  filter(candidate_category == "transmission_upgrade", is_profile_subtype) |>
  left_join(corp_fonsi |> select(project_id, project_title, lead_agency_harmonized, project_state),
            by = "project_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(project_title), nchar(project_title) > 8) |>
  distinct(project_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(desc(within_existing_row), desc(previously_disturbed_land)) |>
  slice_head(n = 6)

tx |>
  transmute(
    Project = str_trunc(project_title, 58),
    Agency = lead_agency_harmonized,
    State = project_state,
    `Within existing ROW` = ifelse(within_existing_row, "yes", "—"),
    `FONSI page` = citation_page
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Sample transmission-upgrade FONSIs (BLM / DOE / PMA)",
             subtitle = "Same in-corridor work TVA already excludes — handled here via full EA") |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12))
```

*(Action descriptions and exact size limits — line length, voltage, acreage —
are extracted but still noisy in this deterministic pass; they are firmed up in
the verification step before any limit is cited to the client.)*

## Is "adopt" realistic? Yes — the CE body is already shared

Adopting another agency's CE is not unusual; it is how the existing CE landscape
already works. Of the `r comma(n_ce)` existing CEs, **`r n_xdup` are near-identical
to a CE at a *different* agency**, forming **`r n_xclust` action-families shared
across two or more agencies**:

```{r cluster-table}
clusters |>
  filter(n_agencies >= 2) |>
  arrange(desc(n_agencies), desc(n_ces)) |>
  slice_head(n = 7) |>
  transmute(
    `Shared action (representative CE text)` = str_trunc(representative_desc, 80),
    `# agencies` = n_agencies,
    Agencies = str_trunc(agencies, 60)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Action categories already excluded by multiple agencies",
             subtitle = glue("{n_xclust} cross-agency CE families in the existing catalog")) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12))
```

Most of the largest shared families are administrative (procurement, personnel,
routine maintenance) — but that is the point: when an action is genuinely
low-impact, agencies routinely converge on the same CE. The clean-energy actions
above are simply ones where that convergence **hasn't happened yet**.

## Where genuinely-new CEs would come from

Net-new CEs are empty here *by construction*: the five candidate action types we
hand-picked are all well-trodden, so all are already CE'd. But recall the funnel —
of the `r n_clean` clean-energy FONSIs, only `r n_candidate` fell into those five
types. The remaining **~`r n_other`** are *other* clean-energy actions we have not
yet categorized. **Net-new CEs most likely live there.** The recommended next
step is to cluster those un-categorized FONSI action descriptions to surface
recurring categories nobody has hand-picked.

## Wind — a discrimination check

Wind (onshore) is kept only as a **contrast**, not a recommendation. The single
existing wind CE (DOE B5.18) covers a *very* small footprint — generally no more
than two turbines under 200 feet. Utility-scale wind (the
`r verdicts$n_observed_fonsi[verdicts$candidate_category=="wind_onshore"]` FONSIs
we see) involves large footprints and case-specific wildlife mitigation, so it
correctly does **not** surface as a CE candidate. This shows the method
discriminates rather than green-lighting everything clean-energy.

## Caveats & next steps

- **Deterministic first pass.** Action definitions and numeric limits are
  directional until the LLM-assisted extraction/verification pass runs; this
  report leads with the structural finding (adopt, not new), which does not
  depend on those specifics.
- **CE matches are a ranking aid, not verified coverage.** Confirm each candidate
  CE against its eCFR text before acting on it.
- **Recommended next steps:** (1) verify the four adopt matches against the eCFR
  CE text; (2) run the verification pass to firm up the transmission size limits;
  (3) cluster the ~`r n_other` un-categorized clean-energy FONSIs to search for
  net-new CEs.

**For CATF:** tell us which of these adopt opportunities to pursue, and whether to
launch the net-new search — and we fold your direction into the next iteration.
